target: For arbitrary n>=1, determine indexed two-step Ore structure of word-quadratic AS-regular Z-domains with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3). Unconditional exhaustion is proved for n=1,2,3. The n=3 proof derives all numerical data, normal-z period two, AS3 and period one of the pure base, and the full indexed Ore flag. For every n, AS regularity of the pure jump-one base B suffices without further numerical/noetherian assumptions. The remaining unconditional exhaustion range is n>=4; final A descent and indexed isomorphism classification remain separate questions.

scope.broad_target: Secondary n=2 target Q: primitive jumps (1,1,2,3), word-quadratic, two-sided AS4 and polynomial row/column growth over the standing algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. Word-Koszulity, AS translation +7, seven-periodicity and the standard relation counts and Hilbert series are proved, not assumed. Domain, noetherianity and period one are not imposed on this secondary all-Q target.
scope.standard_exhaustiveness: Q=H=S. The outer relation counts r_2=r_5=1 have a non-computational proof. The mixed counts r_3=r_4=2 follow from analytically derived necessary conditions and an exact finite integer elimination of the remaining rank arrays. This is a computer-assisted proof under the AS hypotheses, not certification of AS-regularity from low-degree Hilbert agreement. Automatic domainness and period one remain open.
scope.graded_ore_locus: Over C: connected locally finite left/right noetherian AS4 graded algebras with minimal generator degrees (1,1,2,3) and H(t)=1/((1-t)^2(1-t^2)(1-t^3)), classified up to graded isomorphism; relations need not be word-quadratic
scope.quadratic_graded_ore_locus: The word-quadratic part of the preceding graded locus admits a complete Ore chart allowing non-diagonal automorphisms. Its associated Z-algebras lie in H and are 1-periodic; bare indexed isomorphism is a coarser relation.
scope.general_weights: For n>=1: connected locally finite left/right noetherian AS-regular graded C-algebras with minimal generator degrees (1^n,2,3), global dimension n+2, and H(t)=1/((1-t)^n(1-t^2)(1-t^3)).
scope.general_weights_quadratic: Within the stated general-n noetherian graded Hilbert class, word-quadratic algebras are word-Koszul with relation counts (binom(n,2),n,n,1); domain objects admit the exhaustive canonical two-step Ore classification and explicit graded-isomorphism orbits. These are the hypotheses of that graded theorem, not additional assumptions authorized for the arbitrary-n indexed target. Indexed Ore exhaustion is now established independently for n=1,2,3. Universal indexed descent to one graded algebra is false by GEN-INDEXED-PERIOD-TWO, a special case of the n=1 classification; n=2 retains its stronger domain descent theorem. General non-word-quadratic graded exhaustion is not proved for n>=3.
scope.indexed_domain_locus: All Z-domains in Q have standard relation counts and Hilbert series, admit a word-preserving period-one structure, and are associated Z-algebras of B[z;sigma][w;tau,D] over quantum or Jordan planes. Hilbert series, noetherianity and period one are conclusions. A finite matrix criterion now decides existence of bare indexed isomorphisms; orbit normal forms, stabilizers, components and specializations for the full Ore locus remain to be described.
scope.non_domain_boundary: In the secondary n=2 target Q, objects of least period seven or with nonconstant rho_i must have zero divisors. Their existence, projection degeneracy and automatic domainness remain open. This statement is specific to n=2 and is not contradicted by the n=1 domain counterexample with alternating rho. Nonstandard numerical types in Q have been excluded by TYPE-EXHAUST.
scope.domain_regularity_criterion: For a chosen word-homogeneous quadratic presentation of any A in Q, A is a Z-domain if and only if the jump-2, word-length-one generators z_i are left and right regular for i=0,...,6. Each regularity condition concerns multiplication in every degree. Seven-periodicity reduces the indices, not the degrees, so this is not a finite-degree computational test.
scope.pure_degree_one_dichotomy: For every A in Q, without a domain assumption, the excess-zero pure jump-1 subalgebra B has a length-at-most-two simple resolution and endpoint recurrence. Seven-step monodromy first gives the alternative r_2(i)=1 for every i or width at most 13. The finite-width alternative is subsequently excluded by OUTER-RELATION-RANKS; it is no longer an open AS locus.
scope.indexed_isomorphism_criterion: For established domain Ore data (r,S,M,c,L) and (r_prime,S_prime,M_prime,c_prime,L_prime), set T=M S^(-1), J=c^(-1) M^2 S^(-3), lambda=c/c_prime and P_i=T_prime^(-i) P T^i. Bare indexed-isomorphism existence is equivalent to existence of P in GL_2(k) and kappa in k^* satisfying J_prime P=P J, (P tensor P_1)r in k^* r_prime, L_prime P_3=kappa L and L_prime P_4=kappa lambda L. This assumes valid AS/domain Ore data and is not an AS-regularity test or a description of all nonlinear isomorphisms.
scope.diagonal_indexed_classification: For the normalized diagonal quantum three-torus of parameters (a,b,c), bare indexed isomorphism classes are precisely the orbits of the involution (a,b,c)->(a^(-1),b^(-1),c*a^3/b^2). All special values are included; its fixed locus is a=1 and b=+/-1 with c arbitrary nonzero. The finite quotient has dimension 3. This classifies the diagonal family, not the whole domain Ore locus or Q.
scope.outer_relation_ranks: Over the standing algebraically closed field, every A in Q has r_2(i)=r_5(i)=1 and dim B_{i,i+n}=n+1 for its pure jump-1 subalgebra B. This needs neither domainness nor noetherianity. Zero-relation edges in the hypothetical finite-width branch split tensor chains into blocks with at most one two-dimensional relation space; nonzero product covectors extend across the remaining one-dimensional constraints and contradict finite width. Domainness of B or A does not follow from this result alone. MIXED-RELATION-RANKS separately fixes the remaining relation counts.
scope.mixed_relation_ranks: For all Q, r_3(i)=r_4(i)=2. Positivity of the folded Hilbert matrix and divergence of its pure jump-1 part force det P(1,v) identically zero. Its first coefficient forces sum_i(r_3(i)-2)=0; a weight-four cubic-syzygy bound forces r_3(i)+r_3(i+1)<=5. An exact integer check of det P(1,1) over the 890 arrays delta in {-2,-1,0,1,2}^7 with sum zero and delta_i+delta_(i+1)<=1 leaves only delta=0. All assumptions and the matrix orientation are proved before enumeration. Neither projection nondegeneracy nor regularity of z_i is inferred from the ranks.
scope.general_indexed_target: For n>=1 over the standing algebraically closed characteristic-zero field: positive connected locally finite word-quadratic Z-domains with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3), two-sided AS dimension n+2, finitely generated finite projective resolutions of simples, and polynomial row/column growth. No standard Hilbert, noetherian, Koszul or period-one assumption is built into this target.
scope.general_indexed_descent: The universal claim that every object of the arbitrary-n target is the associated Z-algebra of a single graded two-step Ore algebra is false. In the complete n=1 classification, descent occurs exactly when alpha^2=c beta^2, including the zero pair. GEN-INDEXED-PERIOD-TWO is the choice (c,alpha,beta)=(1,1,0), even with standard Hilbert series, word-Koszulity, left/right noetherianity and domainness. The n=2 domain descent theorem remains valid. General descent conditions remain unresolved for n>=3.
scope.general_indexed_ore: Unconditional indexed two-step Ore exhaustion is proved for n=1,2,3 under the original AS/domain/growth hypotheses. For all n, GEN-AS-BASE-ORE proves it from the sole extra AS condition on the pure jump-one base B and its finite two-sided resolutions; no Koszul/H/noetherian/initial-rank/period-one assumptions are added. N3-INDEXED-ORE derives B-AS3 using PERIOD2-BASE-AS3 rather than imposing it. The remaining unconditional range is n>=4. Final A period-one descent is not included in the n3 theorem.
scope.general_indexed_counterexample: The choice (c,alpha,beta)=(1,1,0) in N1-INDEXED-CLASSIFICATION gives epsilon_(2j)=1 and epsilon_(2j+1)=0, with relations z_i x_(i+2)=x_i z_(i+1), w_i z_(i+3)=z_i w_(i+2), and w_i x_(i+3)=x_i w_(i+1)+epsilon_i z_i z_(i+2). It is a word-Koszul, left/right noetherian AS3 Z-domain with AS translation 6, standard two-variable Hilbert series and least positive period 2. The zz-projection rank of R_4 alternates, obstructing period one and hence any presentation as check(D) for a single graded D.
scope.general_indexed_translation: AS Frobenius duality gives a translation i->i+L and a word-preserving A isomorphic to A(L) for arbitrary n, without assuming Koszulity. Directed reachability identifies the vertex order, and E^1,E^2 with their product recover the quadratic presentation. This does not determine L=n+5 or prove word-Koszulity.
scope.general_normal_z_conditional: For arbitrary n, if all r_3(i)=n and r_5(i)=1 and all z_i are left/right regular, the mixed relation projections are isomorphisms, the z_i form a regular normal family, and A(2) is isomorphic to A. Domainness alone gives r_3<=n, r_5<=1 and r_6=0. Attainment of the upper bounds is proved for n=1,2,3 but not established for n>=4.
scope.one_heavy_frobenius_conditional: Indexed non-Koszul one-heavy lemma: Q=T_Z(V direct_sum kw)/(R direct_sum S), V jump one, w jump d>1, R pure V and S in Vw direct_sum wV. If Q is AS(n+1) and B=T_Z(V)/(R) itself is ASn with finite two-sided AS resolutions, then Q=B[w;mu] for an isomorphism B(d)->B. No Koszul, noetherian, prescribed Hilbert or Q-domain assumption. The full Yoneda algebra and its internal degrees, not only the quadratic dual, are used.
scope.one_light_indexed_ore: Every object of Q_1^dom admits a two-step indexed Ore presentation without extra Hilbert, noetherian or Koszul assumptions. AS3 and word-quadraticity force top word length 3 and word-Koszulity; domainness gives r_2=r_6=0; AS duality forces translation 6 and r_3=r_4=r_5=1. The top tensor forces both mixed coefficients of R_4 to be nonzero, and Euler Hilbert series plus ordered spanning gives a PBW basis. Standard Hilbert series and left/right noetherianity are conclusions.
scope.one_light_indexed_classification: Every Q_1^dom object has a normalized presentation z_i x_(i+2)=x_i z_(i+1), w_i z_(i+3)=c z_i w_(i+2), w_i x_(i+3)=x_i w_(i+1)+d_i z_i z_(i+2), where c is nonzero, d_(2j)=c^(-j) alpha and d_(2j+1)=c^(-j) beta. Every parameter triple gives a word-Koszul, left/right noetherian AS3 Z-domain with standard Hilbert series, verified using explicit left/right resolutions. Bare indexed isomorphism is equivalent to c_prime=c and (alpha_prime,beta_prime)=s(alpha,beta) for a nonzero scalar s. For each c the SET of classes is {0} disjoint_union P^1(k), without an affine-quotient or moduli-space assertion. Period one holds exactly when alpha^2=c beta^2, including the zero pair; otherwise the least positive period is two.
scope.three_light_numerics: For every Q_3^dom, top word length N=5, AS translation L=8, word-Koszulity, all relation counts (3,3,3,1,0), H_i(u,t)=1/((1-ut)^3(1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)), regular normal z and A(2) isomorphic to A are proved without extra H/noetherian/Koszul/period assumptions. The pure jump-one domain B has two-sided linear (1,3,3,1) resolutions and H_B=(1-t)^(-3), and PERIOD2-BASE-AS3 separately proves its AS3 property; this is not inferred from numerical ranks alone.
scope.as_base_ore_conditional: For every Q_n^dom, if the pure jump-one subalgebra B itself is ASn with finite two-sided AS resolutions, then r_3=r_4=n, r_5=1, r_6=0 and A is an indexed two-step Ore extension of B. B has period one. For its AS index L_B, one has N_A=L_B+2, L_A=L_B+5 and H_A(u,t)=H_B0(ut)/((1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)). A is word-Koszul iff B is Koszul. Even L_B implies period one of A. General noetherianity or unconditional B-AS is not claimed.
scope.general_r5_growth: For a word-quadratic positive Z-algebra with r_6=0, L-periodic r_5 and polynomial row growth: if 3 does not divide L, r_5(i)+r_5(i-3)>0 and at least ceil(L/2) positions are nonzero. If 3 divides L, at least ceil(L/6) positions are nonzero. In a domain r_5<=1, so the position bounds are sum bounds. The monomial quotient test alone does not exclude alternating missing R5 for L=2; no AS-domain realization of that pattern is asserted.
scope.period_two_base_recognition: Any positive connected locally finite, adjacent-generated quadratic Z-domain with an algebra period B(2) isomorphic to B and dim B_(i,i+m)=binom(m+2,2) is two-sided Koszul and AS-regular of global dimension three with AS translation +3. Koszulity, finite global dimension, noetherianity and period one are not assumed. Quadratic presentation/Hilbert/domain give exact 1331 complexes. The two-vertex fold embeds faithfully in a fraction division category; all rank-(2,2) top tensors are excluded by dimensions of alternating products and rational-function pole growth. Nondegenerate top pairings and the Koszul bimodule resolution give AS duality and global dimension for all unital modules. No ordinary classification is used.
scope.three_light_indexed_ore: Every Q_3^dom admits C=B[z;sigma], A=C[w;theta,delta] as indexed Ore extensions, with sigma:B(2)->B and theta:C(3)->C isomorphisms. B is a quadratic AS3 Z-domain and has period one; A has period two and AS translation eight. Relations are z_i v=sigma_i(v)z_(i+1), w_i v=mu_i(v)w_(i+1)+L_i(v)z_i z_(i+2), w_i z_(i+3)=c_i z_i w_(i+2), with sigma_i,mu_i invertible and c_i nonzero. Ordered B z^a w^b components form PBW bases. No additional H/noetherian/Koszul/period assumption is made. Final A period one and full indexed orbit classification are not proved.
scope.three_light_derivation_support: In the n3 indexed Ore presentation, either all L_i vanish or all are nonzero. Applying delta to the base relations and using their full left/right support makes L_i=0 equivalent to L_(i+1)=0. In the all-zero case w is a regular normal family, so A has period three; combined with period two it has period one. Descent for the all-nonzero branch remains unresolved.

Over C, connected locally finite left/right noetherian AS4, prescribed Hilbert series and minimal degrees (1,1,2,3): all and only iterated Ore extensions of a quantum or Jordan plane. No claim for all Q.
Finite necessary and sufficient coefficient equations for the graded Ore data; contains all special parameter values.
All graded isomorphisms are the specified triangular changes satisfying explicit equations; not a classification of bare indexed isomorphisms.

Within the stated noetherian graded Hilbert locus over C: the full word-quadratic Ore chart, allowing non-diagonal automorphisms. Graded-isomorphism existence is characterized in prop:quadratic-isomorphisms; the displayed zero-correction conditions use generators adapted to a word-quadratic presentation.
No word-quadratic or domain assumption: AS index n+5 and weighted Tor_i supported in i..i+3, under the stated noetherian global-dimension and Hilbert hypotheses.

All n in the word-quadratic Hilbert locus, without a domain assumption: word-Koszul with word Hilbert series (1-u)^(-n-2), canonical B Koszul of global dimension n and H_B=(1-t)^(-n), relation counts (binom(n,2),n,n,1). B AS-Gorenstein is not claimed at this stage. Domain additionally gives a regular normal degree-2 generator.

All n: exhaustive two-step Ore data for left/right noetherian domains, AS dimension n+2, prescribed Hilbert series and word-quadratic minimal generators. The canonical base B is an n-dimensional AS-regular domain with ordinary polynomial Hilbert series. Proof of exhaustion in thm:quadratic-all-ones uses noetherian finite generation in A/(z), not an assumed domain property of that quotient.

Necessary and sufficient finite coefficient conditions over any base in B_n, including non-word-quadratic homogeneous relations. This is the specified Ore family, not an exhaustion of the general homogeneous locus.
All graded isomorphisms in the general Ore family are triangular and satisfy the displayed conditions; no claim for bare indexed isomorphisms.
Existence of a graded isomorphism between quadratic charts is equivalent to the stated linear orbit condition. Actual isomorphisms may be nonlinear.
A genuine graded double Ore extension over a degree-one-generated base with minimal weights 2 and 3 is an iterated automorphism Ore extension in that order.

Fixed minimal degrees (1^n,2,3) admit noetherian AS-regular domains of global dimension n+m+2 for all m>=0. For m>=1 the canonical first Ore step fails; these examples do not have the prescribed n+2-dimensional Hilbert profile.
B -> B[z,w] is injective on graded isomorphism classes of ordinary AS-regular polynomial-Hilbert bases; domain bases map into the quadratic domain locus.

Explicit Sklyanin S(1,2,1)[z2,w3] lies in the strong quadratic n=3 locus but is not an iterated graded Ore extension from k on its five minimal generators; its canonical two-step Ore flag over S exists.

For Z-domains in Q, the jump-2, word-length-one generator family is regular normal and induces an isomorphism of the full Z-algebra with its two-vertex translate. Standard relation dimensions are derived in DOMAIN-STANDARD rather than imposed.

All Z-domains in Q, without a noetherian or Hilbert-series hypothesis: relation counts (1,2,2,1,0), standard Koszul resolutions and the prescribed two-variable Hilbert series. The proof sums seven Euler identities and uses domain injections to compare row series.

All Z-domains in Q are period one and associated to a connected graded domain with a compatible word grading. Period two and period seven imply period one; commuting periodicity maps are not required.

All Z-domains in Q are associated Z-algebras of two-step Ore extensions B[z;sigma][w;tau,D] over quantum or Jordan planes. Noetherianity, the standard Hilbert series and period one are conclusions. The AS3 quotient syzygy proves normality of w before quotient domainness is inferred. This strengthening is for n=2, not arbitrary n; the structural exhaustion is supplemented by ORE-FULL-ISOM, a finite existence criterion. Full orbit normal forms and geometry remain open.

Every least-period-seven object or object with nonconstant rho_i in Q has zero divisors. No existence claim for these loci and no proof that all Q is a domain. Nonstandard Hilbert and relation-count types have been excluded independently by TYPE-EXHAUST.

For all Q and a chosen word-quadratic presentation, Z-domainness is equivalent to two-sided regularity of the jump-2, word-length-one generators z_0,...,z_6 in all degrees. The proof first obtains standard ranks and periods two and one using z-regularity alone; it then derives noetherianity from the AS3 normal quotient and only subsequently derives domainness. This is a finite-index reduction, not a finite-degree test.

A positive two-periodic Z-domain of polynomial growth folds to a two-object category whose nonzero morphisms admit faithful localization. Corner polynomial-growth domains are Ore because disjoint principal ideals would produce exponential binary-word growth. Nonzero return arrows supply common multiples for different targets. A nonzero arrow frame puts X,Y in one division ring while preserving all alternating products and dimensions.

Any positive connected locally finite, adjacent-generated quadratic Z-domain with an algebra period B(2) isomorphic to B and dim B_(i,i+m)=binom(m+2,2) is two-sided Koszul and AS-regular of global dimension three with AS translation +3. Koszulity, finite global dimension, noetherianity and period one are not assumed. Quadratic presentation/Hilbert/domain give exact 1331 complexes. The two-vertex fold embeds faithfully in a fraction division category; all rank-(2,2) top tensors are excluded by dimensions of alternating products and rational-function pole growth. Nondegenerate top pairings and the Koszul bimodule resolution give AS duality and global dimension for all unital modules. No ordinary classification is used.

Every Q_3^dom admits C=B[z;sigma], A=C[w;theta,delta] as indexed Ore extensions, with sigma:B(2)->B and theta:C(3)->C isomorphisms. Relations are z_i v=sigma_i(v)z_(i+1), w_i v=mu_i(v)w_(i+1)+L_i(v)z_i z_(i+2), w_i z_(i+3)=c_i z_i w_(i+2), with sigma_i,mu_i invertible and c_i nonzero. Ordered B z^a w^b components form PBW bases. No additional H/noetherian/Koszul/period assumption is made. Final A period one and full indexed orbit classification are not proved.

In the n3 indexed Ore presentation, either all L_i vanish or all are nonzero. Applying delta to the base relations and using their full left/right support makes L_i=0 equivalent to L_(i+1)=0. In the all-zero case w is a regular normal family, so A has period three; combined with period two it has period one. Descent for the all-nonzero branch remains unresolved.

open_problems.problem: For n>=4, derive AS regularity of the pure jump-one base B or find a counterexample. GEN-AS-BASE-ORE already provides the complete indexed Ore construction from B-AS alone. Unconditional exhaustion is proved for n1,n2,n3; do not reopen the n3 base-AS step. No additional H/Koszul/noetherian/period assumption is authorized.

Use the excess-zero bar complex, folded Hilbert comparisons and GEN-R5-GROWTH; the latter alone permits some missing-relation patterns. Do not assume L=n+5 or Koszulity.

Its proof uses three-dimensional support intersections and 3-by-2 Segre bounds, so those steps cannot be transferred by replacing the number of generators. General AS-base Ore gives A period two and period L_B+5, hence period one if L_B is even; a Koszul base with even n is a special case. N3 has L_A=8 and period two, which do not force A period one. Secondary n=2 question; domainness is permitted in the current main problem and need not be proved first. Determine whether every object of Q is a Z-domain by the equivalent condition that the seven jump-2, word-length-one generators z_0,...,z_6 of a chosen word-quadratic presentation have zero left and right annihilators in every degree. All relation counts and Hilbert series are now standard. Begin with kernels of the two projections of R_3 and vanishing coefficients of the one-dimensional R_5, then control possible higher-degree annihilators using AS duality and exact Koszul resolutions. Under the proved standard relation dimensions, determine whether degenerate mixed projections can occur in Q. Analyze the Vz/zV projections of the two-dimensional R_3 and the Vw/wV/zz projections of the two-dimensional R_4; do not assume the two coefficients of the one-dimensional R_5 are nonzero. The relation counts themselves and Q=H=S are already proved. R5-ORIENTATION-OBSTRUCTION excludes opposite one-sided relations at relative distances 2,3,4 modulo 7; focus on remaining distances 1,5,6 and configurations with only one orientation.

Use the proved finite necessary-and-sufficient criterion ORE-FULL-ISOM to obtain normal forms, stabilizers, components and specializations for general quantum- or Jordan-plane Ore data. Determine structural branches and necessary/sufficient AS and Koszul conditions inside the fixed standard-rank seven-window parameter space, especially candidates with zero divisors. All actual objects of Q have relation counts (1,2,2,1). The mixed-rank computation excludes other rank arrays under AS hypotheses; it does not certify AS-regularity of arbitrary candidates. Finite Frobenius duality alone is also insufficient.
Construct or exclude objects of Q with least period seven; any such object has zero divisors. Domain Ore families cannot supply such examples.

Classify all standard-rank objects Q=H=S up to indexed isomorphism and determine irreducible components, specializations, stabilizers and relative descent, including any zero-divisor loci. Numerical type exhaustion is complete. The diagonal quantum family has a proved dimension-three finite quotient; do not extrapolate this to the whole Ore or AS parameter space.

For n>=3 and fixed global dimension n+2 and prescribed Hilbert series, determine whether arbitrary weighted-homogeneous relations admit the canonical iterated Ore flag. First analyze n=3 augmentation initial relations without assuming the associated graded algebra remains quadratic or AS-regular.
